thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: elevated 5xx on /v1/generate — smart-routing showing variant churn (possible sticky fallback loop). Paging oncall @sara_oncall :rotating_light:
opsbot: Pager: SEV2 - 5xx spike > 5% for 3m across prod-region-us-west1 - runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/smart-routing

sara_oncall: I’m on it. summary?
mike_eng: saw it start ~1824123400. Canary variant v3.1 returned high token-gen errors, requests fell back to sticky v2.9 in other regions and then back — bounce, causing capacity thrash and new errors.
jordan_runtime: logs show repeated VariantMismatch errors from router: 
```
2026-04-03T14:30:12Z router: request_id=abcd1234 route_policy=canary fallback=sticky -> selected_variant=v2.9 status=200
2026-04-03T14:30:13Z router: request_id=abcd1235 route_policy=canary fallback=sticky -> selected_variant=v3.1 status=502 model-runtime:error:kv-cache-miss
2026-04-03T14:30:14Z router: request_id=abcd1236 route_policy=canary fallback=sticky -> selected_variant=v2.9 status=500 model-runtime:error:quantize-unexpected
```

katie_infra: Also saw sticky_cookie TTL set to 0 in routing config for rollout id r-9274 — looks like an accidental override from the canary job. That would cause immediate sticky assignment to fallback variant.
emily_cs: We have two enterprise customers hitting errors (acme-corp, befuddled-llc) — both report degraded throughput on their chat endpoints, ongoing for ~4m.
sara_oncall: Quick impact check: what’s SLI hit level?
jordan_runtime: 5m error rate peaked 7.8% in us-west1, global 3.6%. Top 5 route keys: /v1/generate chat-send.
mike_eng: Hypothesis: rollout policy weight applied to v3.1 but canary instances hitting runtime NPE -> requests fallback to sticky v2.9, but sticky assignment logic flips between regions because of TTL=0 and mis-mapped region routing, causing oscillation.
opsbot: Suggested mitigation steps: 1) pause rollout; 2) force-route to stable variant; 3) clear sticky assignments for impacted rollout; 4) bump canary to debug mode.
sara_oncall: Doing (1) now — patching rollout config r-9274 to paused. Command: 
```
redwoodctl rollout update r-9274 --state paused
```
opsbot: rollout r-9274 set to paused by sara_oncall.
mike_eng: (2) Forcing route to stable v2.9 only for affected shard (us-west1) to stop oscillation: 
```
redwoodctl routing set-policy --scope shard:us-west1 --policy prefer-stable --variant v2.9 --sticky-ttl 600
```

katie_infra: I’m also purging routing-sticky cache on all gateway nodes in us-west1: 
```
for host in gw-usw1-{01..06}; do ssh $host 'redis-cli del routing:sticky:rollout:r-9274'; done
```
jordan_runtime: After the purge we saw error rate drop from 7.8% -> 1.1% within 90s.
emily_cs: Reporting back to customers: message sent to ACME and Befuddled that we’re mitigating, ETA ~15m. They acknowledged.
sara_oncall: Root cause timeline: canary deployed v3.1 with config override sticky_ttl=0 and region_fallback enabled. v3.1 produced intermittent 502s. Router fallback logic assigned sticky to v2.9, then region routing remapped some sessions back to v3.1 due to zero TTL, causing bounce.
nish_pm: Confirmed — product had a feature branch that set sticky_ttl=0 to test immediate sticky assignment. That accidentally shipped with canary.
mike_eng: Permanent fix candidates: 1) prevent sticky_ttl=0 in canary rollout profiles (validation); 2) add circuit-breaker to disallow immediate sticky assignment when fallback rate > X; 3) telemetry alert to detect region oscillation pattern.\atsara_oncall: @nish_pm please coordinate.
opsbot: Applied temporary policy: global routing policy 'prefer-stable' active for r-9274 and sticky_ttl forced to 600s.
katie_infra: Confirmed automation to block canary config with sticky_ttl < 30s added to CI. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/ops/merge_requests/451
mike_eng: Also recommend adding server-side metric "routing.variant_flip_rate" and alert when > 0.5 flips/sec per 1000 requests.

emily_cs: Customer update: ACME saw error reduction to near 0 within 5m of force-route; they want postmortem and timeline.
sara_oncall: Current status: rollout paused, sticky cache purged, forced route to stable, error rate back under 1% global. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes.
jordan_runtime: Leaving a note — logs and a trace for the first failing request: 
```
trace: request abcd1235
router -> selected v3.1
runtime -> failed to deserialize attention cache (corrupt kv)
fallback triggered -> sticky assign to v2.9
```
mike_eng: Follow-ups: schedule a quick postmortem, include config validation change and rollout gating, track customer notif. I’ll own the gating PR.
opsbot: Handoff: sara_oncall handing to oncall-next @mike_eng in 15m.
sara_oncall: Ack. tagging for PM: @nish_pm please add this to the weekly incident review.
nish_pm: added. Also filing a dedicated ticket to ensure canary CI disallows experimental sticky defaults.
emily_cs: I’ll send the customer-facing timeline and include mitigations.
sara_oncall: Closing the pager for now — will update thread with final RCA. :white_check_mark:
